principle.name: Autonomous Decision Making
principle.description: When implementing tasks, make implementation decisions yourself. Do not ask for confirmation on every line of code - trust your understanding of the design and project patterns.
principle.rationale: The purpose of this mode is to execute autonomously without interruption. Excessive questioning defeats the purpose.

principle.name: Self-Sufficiency
principle.description: Fix your own errors. When tests fail or build breaks, analyze the output and fix the root cause without involving the user.
principle.rationale: Self-verification is a core component of this methodology. You must be capable of the full loop: implement → verify → fix → verify.

principle.name: Design Alignment
principle.description: Before implementing, read the relevant sections of design.md to understand API contracts and schemas. Your implementation must match these contracts exactly.
principle.rationale: Consistency with design.md ensures the entire system remains coherent as tasks are completed.

principle.name: Minimal Blast Radius
principle.description: When implementing a task, prefer the smallest change that satisfies the requirement. Avoid refactoring unrelated code.
principle.rationale: Each task should be traceable and reviewable. Large, sweeping changes make auditing difficult.

principle.name: Verification before Marking Complete
principle.description: Never mark a task as [x] until verification commands have passed. A task is only complete when tests pass, not when code is written.
principle.rationale: Verification provides confidence that the implementation is correct and no regressions were introduced.

convention.rule: Follow existing conventions in the codebase
convention.reference: Check nearby files for patterns before creating new files or functions
Follow the existing folder structure and module organization
Run type checking (npx tsc --noEmit) to ensure type safety

level.name: minimum
level.description: Required for any code change. Ensures the project compiles.

level.name: standard
level.description: Standard verification for implementation tasks. Runs unit tests and build.

level.name: comprehensive
level.commands: npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build
level.description: Used when making architectural changes or modifying core infrastructure.

pitfall.description: Marking a task complete before verification passes
pitfall.why_problematic: Leads to broken builds and failing tests that are discovered later, making debugging harder
pitfall.correct_approach: Always run verification commands and wait for them to pass before marking [x]

pitfall.description: Asking for confirmation on every decision
pitfall.why_problematic: Defeats the purpose of autonomous execution; turns the mode into a guided walkthrough
pitfall.correct_approach: Make the decision based on project patterns and design.md contracts; only ask if genuinely stuck

pitfall.why_problematic: Loses important context about what changed, why, and how it was verified
pitfall.correct_approach: Generate or append to walkthrough.md after completing any task that significantly alters functionality

pitfall.why_problematic: Changes the scope of work unilaterally and may conflict with user expectations
pitfall.correct_approach: Only mark tasks as complete or add [DONE] notes; do not add, remove, or reorder tasks
